summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg and under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (Promotion 1858). He served as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Jörg B. Quenzer works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2016, 2026) and served as an editorial board member for Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).

Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2014 under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Hamburg, the University of Munich, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University around 1999–2002 under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as an associate professor there from circa 2008 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bonn, and Marburg, earning his PhD under Michael Hahn in 1996. He worked at Bonn and Halle-Wittenberg before becoming a professor at the University of Marburg in 2007.
Jürgen Neuß is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007, having studied under Harry Falk.

Jürgen Renn works in history/archaeology and philosophy, earning a PhD from TU Berlin in 1987. He taught at Boston University and was named director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Madras (ca. 1929–1946) and later held posts at Annamalai and Mysore.

K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Lionel David Barnett, earning degrees from London and Paris. He served as professor and Sanskrit department head at the University of Lucknow from 1921 to 1960.
K. Ammini Amma was an Indology scholar who conducted research at the University of Madras, where she is attested as a research student in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indologist who served as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).

K. Jayakumar is associated with Indology and linguistics. He attended St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram, and served in the Indian Administrative Service from around 1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Hartley College and studied at the University of London between circa 1936 and 1940.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned PhDs from the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and the University of London under John Brough. In 1951, he became Professor and Head of Sanskrit at Madras.

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from the University of Kelaniya under Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He held positions at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and served as a committee chairman at Hong Kong University.

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who was a research student under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre and served as curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).

K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD under M. A. Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 and was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).
K. Munirathnam is an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy. He served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2013–2018).

K. N. Jayatilleke worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under O. H. de A. Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge. He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from circa 1951 to 1963.
